messages:
maria: quick design check — I pushed a prototype for the bulk-delete flow. main question: inline validation for each row vs a single destructive confirmation modal. thoughts?

kevin: for bulk delete we need something that scales. modal alone feels fine, but if some rows fail (permissions) inline errors would help people fix without re-running.

olivia: agree. users expect a single final confirm for destructive actions. modal should be the gate, but show inline validation upstream so modal only confirms effective set. :+1:

sam: +1. also accessibility nit: if modal opens focus must go to the input and screen readers should announce context e.g. "Confirm deletion of 12 items". We should avoid relying only on color.

maria: good call. prototype has an optional typed-confirm pattern: require typing the number of items or the word DELETE for >10 items. For smaller sets show a checkbox "I understand this cannot be undone". Trying to balance friction.

kevin: hmm typed-confirm is strong—might be heavy for 2-3 items. maybe threshold at 5+? Also what about keyboard-only users: typed-confirm can be fine but ensure label and aria-describedby explain.

olivia: microcopy suggestion: instead of just "Type DELETE", say "Type DELETE to permanently remove these items" (short). For count-based: "Type the number of items to confirm: 3" helps scannability.

accessibility-bot: automated check: ensure modal has role="dialog", aria-modal="true", aria-labelledby points to modal title, and the confirmation input has aria-label or aria-labelledby plus aria-describedby for error messages.

maria: thanks bot. question about inline error placement: in the bulk table we show a per-row error badge with an inline message that appears beneath the row when validation fails. Is that ok or too noisy?

sam: beneath the row is good for context. keep messages succinct: e.g., "Insufficient permissions — cannot delete". For screen readers, add aria-live="polite" region that reads aggregated failures when the user opens the modal.

kevin: implementation detail: we can compute an "effective set" on backend and show a summary in modal: "9 items will be deleted, 3 cannot be deleted (insufficient permissions)." Provide link "View details" that expands inline list. That avoids forcing users to comb the table first.

olivia: UI tweak: use required marker only on form fields requiring input in modal (e.g., typed-confirm). We should not clutter the table with required asterisks. Also ensure color + star for required fields and non-color indicator for accessibility.

maria: agreed. action items: 1) kevin to add backend summary count + details link, 2) sam to write aria-live copy and modal focus notes, 3) olivia to update microcopy for typed-confirm variants. I'll update prototype and re-share.

kevin: will do — I'll land a small API stub by EOD.

olivia: :thumbsup: a11y and copy look small but make big UX difference here.

maria: thanks team — pushing updated Figma in ~30m.
